Form fields

Text fields, selects and text areas with Bootstrap 5's names: a label floating in the field or above it, a hint, an error said in words, an icon inside the field.

Examples

form-floating keeps the label inside the field and lifts it when the field has a value or the focus. The label follows the control, and the control needs a placeholder - it is how CSS knows the field is empty.

<div class="form-floating">
	<input class="form-control" id="form-floating-name" value="Ang Thong: marine park by speedboat" placeholder="A name people search for">
	<label for="form-floating-name">Name</label>
</div>
<div class="form-floating">
	<input class="form-control" id="form-floating-mail" type="email" placeholder="name@example.com">
	<label for="form-floating-mail">E-mail</label>
</div>
<div class="form-floating">
	<select class="form-select" id="form-floating-section"><option>Marine</option><option>Land</option><option>Evening</option></select>
	<label for="form-floating-section">Section</label>
</div>
<div class="form-floating">
	<textarea class="form-control" id="form-floating-note" placeholder="A note for the guides">Pick up at the pier at 8:30.</textarea>
	<label for="form-floating-note">Note</label>
</div>

A label above, a hint, an error

form-field stacks a field's parts: form-label, the control, form-text for a hint and invalid-feedback for an error. The control points at both with aria-describedby; an error sets aria-invalid="true", and the browser's own :user-invalid draws the same after the person has edited the field.

Full address /excursions/ang-thong/. The old one answers with a 301 redirect.
Lower than the child price
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-stacked-slug">Address</label>
	<input class="form-control font-monospace" id="form-stacked-slug" value="ang-thong" aria-describedby="form-stacked-slug-hint">
	<div class="form-text" id="form-stacked-slug-hint">Full address /excursions/ang-thong/. The old one answers with a 301 redirect.</div>
</div>
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-stacked-price">Adult price, THB</label>
	<input class="form-control tabular-nums" id="form-stacked-price" type="number" value="2500" min="0" step="100" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="form-stacked-price-error">
	<div class="invalid-feedback" id="form-stacked-price-error"><i class="bi bi-exclamation-triangle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i>Lower than the child price</div>
</div>

An icon in the field

form-adorn puts an icon inside a field, at its start; the field keeps its own name. With form-floating on the same element the label starts after the icon, inside the one border - the way a sign-in form draws its fields.

<div class="form-adorn">
	<i class="bi bi-search" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<input class="form-control" type="search" placeholder="Name, slug or code" aria-label="Search excursions">
</div>
<div class="form-floating form-adorn">
	<i class="bi bi-envelope" aria-hidden="true"></i>
	<input class="form-control" id="form-adorn-mail" type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" autocomplete="email">
	<label for="form-adorn-mail">E-mail</label>
</div>
<div class="input-group">
	<div class="form-floating form-adorn">
		<i class="bi bi-key" aria-hidden="true"></i>
		<input class="form-control" id="form-adorn-password" type="password" placeholder="Password" autocomplete="current-password">
		<label for="form-adorn-password">Password</label>
	</div>
	<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" commandfor="form-adorn-password" command="--reveal" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Show the password"><i class="bi bi-eye" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</div>

Sizes

form-control-sm and form-select-sm are 28 px high, the default 32 px, -lg 40 px - the same heights as the buttons beside them.

<input class="form-control form-control-sm" placeholder="Small" aria-label="Small field">
<input class="form-control" placeholder="Default" aria-label="Default field">
<input class="form-control form-control-lg" placeholder="Large" aria-label="Large field">
<select class="form-select form-select-sm" aria-label="Small select"><option>Small select</option></select>

A one-time code

form-control-otp spaces the digits of a code from an app or a message in one field. One field takes a paste and the code the system offers above the keyboard - a box per digit takes neither - and the form goes by its button, never by the last digit.

Spaces and dashes are fine.
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-otp-code">6-digit code from your app</label>
	<input class="form-control form-control-otp" id="form-otp-code" type="text" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code" pattern="[0-9 \-]*" spellcheck="false" enterkeyhint="done" aria-describedby="form-otp-code-hint">
	<div class="form-text" id="form-otp-code-hint">Spaces and dashes are fine.</div>
</div>

A new password

A button with command="--reveal" for a password field shows its text and hides it again - aria-pressed says which - and the field hides it on its form's submit and when the page comes back from the history. Each element with data-strength naming the field shows its level as it is typed: shorter than its minlength, long enough, then longer or of three kinds of characters, then both - a meter at once, and the words, the page's texts strength.short, .fair, .good and .strong, once the typing pauses, said politely by a live region of the field's own - VoiceOver says nothing of a password field's own description changing, so the words' element needs no aria-live. The level is a hint: the server keeps its own rules.

At least 12 characters. A phrase of a few words is easy to remember.
<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-password-new">New password</label>
	<div class="input-group">
		<input class="form-control" id="form-password-new" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" minlength="12" spellcheck="false" aria-describedby="form-password-hint form-password-level">
		<button class="btn btn-icon" type="button" commandfor="form-password-new" command="--reveal" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Show the password"><i class="bi bi-eye" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
	</div>
	<meter class="meter" min="0" max="4" low="2" high="3" optimum="4" value="0" data-strength="form-password-new" aria-label="Password strength"></meter>
	<div class="form-text" id="form-password-level" data-strength="form-password-new"></div>
	<div class="form-text" id="form-password-hint">At least 12 characters. A phrase of a few words is easy to remember.</div>
</div>

A range

form-range on an <input type="range"> is the browser's own slider in the theme's accent: it keeps its keys (the arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down) and its look in forced colors. The label says what it sets; when the number matters, write it beside the slider.

<div class="form-field">
	<label class="form-label" for="form-range-quality">Photo quality</label>
	<input class="form-range" id="form-range-quality" type="range" min="40" max="100" step="5" value="80">
</div>

Keyboard and accessibility

  • Every control has a visible label: a <label for>, or aria-label only where the context says it all - a search field with its icon.
  • A placeholder is never the label: it goes away as the person types. In form-floating the placeholder is only the empty marker.
  • An error is said in words in invalid-feedback, joined to the control by aria-describedby; a color alone never tells it.
  • The borders of fields and the focus ring are at least 3:1 against the page in both themes; the text 4.5:1.
  • form-select paints its own chevron from the theme, mirrored right to left; a multiple select or one with size drops it.
